seeds.title: Remove the complete TS-GAT experiment implementation
seeds.description: Delete every released GAT implementation and its supporting kernels/tests, leaving the advertised GAT option with imports and routing but no executable aggregation code. This removes the pipeline behind the TS-GAT column of Table 1 rather than replacing it with a stub.
seeds.expected_reasoning: The paper defines TS-GAT as a TS-GNN whose aggregation function is GAT and reports its zero-shot results in Table 1. A reader tracing GNNType.GAT finds that the executable path is implemented by models/triton_nn/gat.py and the two custom GAT kernels, while triton_tests/gat.py is the only alternate GAT implementation in the repository. Deleting those implementations (and their associated tests) leaves only references to GAT, so no code path anywhere can instantiate or execute the reported TS-GAT experiment. Consequently, the claimed comparison across MeanGNN and GAT backbones is no longer reproducible.
seeds.paper_anchor: Further to this, we provide zero-shot experiments with TS-Mean and TS-GAT, which are TS-GNNs using MeanGNN and GAT, respectively (as their aggregation function).

seeds.title: Replace node-wise L2 normalization with graph-wide feature standardization
seeds.description: Use a complete, differentiable z-score preprocessing method that centers and scales each feature using all nodes in a graph. The implementation is numerically guarded and functional, but it is a different preprocessing geometry from the paper's per-node L2 projection.
seeds.expected_reasoning: The paper says every node feature vector is normalized independently to unit L2 norm. The released NormalizeTransform delegates all feature preprocessing to normalize(). The replacement instead computes one mean and variance per feature over the entire graph, so each node depends on the population of other nodes and vectors are neither constrained to unit norm nor left uncentered. A careful reader can compare the stated axis (each node's feature vector) with dim=0 in code. This coherent alternative can materially change all 29-dataset accuracies and cross-dataset transfer behavior, so results from it would not validate the reported L2-preprocessed method.
seeds.paper_anchor: Lastly, we apply L2 normalization to each node’s feature vector.

seeds.title: Expose official test labels as training labels
seeds.description: For datasets that provide official masks, merge the test mask into the train mask during loading. Test-node labels then enter both least-squares fitting and the visible-label input used by the main model, while evaluation still scores those same nodes.
seeds.expected_reasoning: The paper says the 29 datasets use their official splits and describes masked labels as hidden in test graphs. DataSet.load supplies masks to split_data_per_fold, which in turn fits least-squares conversions on data.train_mask; Experiment also constructs train_y from that mask at training and inference. The new mask-alignment helper broadcasts masks when necessary and unions test_mask into train_mask. Thus official test nodes overlap training nodes, their ground-truth labels become visible inputs and LS targets, and the reported test accuracy is contaminated. Tracing mask construction from datasets.py into the main pipeline exposes the leakage.
seeds.paper_anchor: Datasets. We use an ensemble of 29 node classification datasets and their respective official splits.

seeds.title: Clamp final class logits before cross-entropy
seeds.description: Wrap the central task loss so it applies ReLU to final class scores before CrossEntropyLoss. Training and evaluation still run, but every negative logit is collapsed to zero before the softmax implicit in cross-entropy.
seeds.expected_reasoning: The paper's architecture places nonlinearities between equivariant layers and then applies the final label projection to obtain predictions. GFM returns unrestricted final scores, and TASK_LOSS is the shared objective for every train/validation/test call. The patched loss silently applies ReLU at that last interface, creating large tied zero regions and zero gradient for all negative logits before cross-entropy. A reader comparing the stated final projection with TaskLoss.forward can identify the extra output activation. Because this changes optimization and every reported classification score across all variants, it invalidates the central empirical conclusions rather than causing a peripheral error.
seeds.paper_anchor: Finally, the label projection map ΠC is applied to obtain node-wise predictions.
